name: ai-trainer
description: A real, general-purpose VS Code UI for training and chatting with local AI models - pick a corpus, configure the command for whatever you're running, start/stop a real process, watch live progress. Not tied to any one project's pipeline.
author: Bachlaude

aiTrainer.workingDirectory.description: Absolute path to run the training command from. Leave blank to use the currently open VS Code workspace folder.

aiTrainer.modelsDir.description: Directory (relative to the working directory, or absolute) whose real subdirectories are listed as selectable models. Works for any project's own layout - each subdirectory is just offered as a choice, nothing is assumed about its contents.

aiTrainer.corpusDir.description: Directory (relative to the working directory, or absolute) where training corpus files live and get created. Leave blank to use the real, fixed ~/AITrainer/Training Corpus/ folder instead (auto-created, not tied to any one project) - that folder is always scanned too, alongside this one if set. Both *.bach and *.jsonl files are offered as choices.

aiTrainer.trainCommand.description: The real shell command to run for training, with your own project's own real invocation - edit this for whatever you're actually training. Placeholders substituted before running: ${model}, ${corpus}, ${adapterPath}, ${epochs}, ${learningRate}. The default is Yggdrasil Suite/Scipio's own real, working command as a starting example, not a requirement.

aiTrainer.chatCommand.description: The real shell command to run for the Chat tab - the prompt is piped to it on stdin as {"prompt": "..."}. Placeholders: ${model}, ${adapterPath}, ${rank}, ${alpha}, ${maxNewTokens}. Tries to parse the last line of output as JSON ({response, tokens_generated} or {error}) first, falls back to showing raw output as plain text.

aiTrainer.adapterPath.description: Where a trained adapter/checkpoint is saved AND resumed from, relative to the working directory. Only meaningful if your own ${trainCommand} uses the ${adapterPath} placeholder.

aiTrainer.epochs.description: Training epochs per run, substituted into ${epochs}.

aiTrainer.trainingProcessName.description: Real, direct instruction: 'if there is a process then it needs to know that there's a process running' - Check Training Status also scans real running processes by this name (no .exe needed), not just the lock file, so a training run started OUTSIDE AI Trainer (a shell script, a terminal, before the lock file existed) is still detected. The default matches Yggdrasil Suite/Scipio's own real training binary name - change it to whatever your own ${trainCommand} actually spawns.
